clue.text: Pass English, covering stage in educational institution

indicators.note: the first pieces spread round the stage, holding it between them

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A student scrapes through English while also doing a stage of a course at some school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as succeeding in a subject, but it is a mountain pass; 'covering' has the outer pieces enclose the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of further or higher learning, a kind of educational institution.

clue.text: A-listers touring Eastern Sulawesi in the past

indicators.note: the celebrities go round the next letter, encircling it

parts.note: celebs are celebrities

explanation.surface: Famous people on a trip round part of Indonesia some years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebes was the former name of the Indonesian island now called Sulawesi.

clue.text: Finer island rocks — here?

indicators.note: the letters are shaken up, as if rocked

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the best island rocky coast is to be found at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is a verb shaking the letters, while the whole clue also describes the rocky tidal isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Island off Northumberland, reached by a causeway, is a rocky island with a famous priory.

clue.text: Pen debut for Shakespeare possibly? Look at this set in Globe

indicators.note: these letters could possibly be arranged another way
the first appearance of the playwright's name is its opening letter

parts.note: 'Here!' is said to draw attention, like 'look at this'

explanation.surface: A first piece of writing by the Bard, displayed at his Globe theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PEN plus S (the debut of Shakespeare) into ENSP. 'Globe' looks like the theatre, but means a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensphere is to enclose in a sphere or orb, so it means placed within a globe.

clue.text: See edifices partly gutted

indicators.note: with the insides removed, only the first and last letters of each word remain

explanation.surface: Look at buildings whose interiors have been half stripped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a literary synonym for spotting something.

clue.text: Match speed in producing clothing accessory

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture in a sports competition
clip means speed, as in 'at a fair clip'

explanation.surface: A sportswriter on how fast a game was played while describing something worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie clip holds a necktie to the shirt front, a small accessory worn with formal clothes.

clue.text: Island's in good order, following behaviour of groups

indicators.note: the island piece goes inside the good-order word

parts.note: in good trim means in good order
Bali is an Indonesian island, so Bali's

explanation.surface: An island kept tidy, after the habits of crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island' is not I here; it is the island BALI, with its 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is loyalty to one's own tribe or faction, the way people act in groups.

clue.text: High sense of self, say, is entrenched in old money

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

indicators.note: the is word is dug deep inside the old money letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Self-importance, for example, is ingrained among the established rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old money' looks like a fixed phrase, but it gives O and M with IS between.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is excessive self-regard, an inflated view of one's own importance.

clue.text: Collection of flowers that is left to come up

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters rise, reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A bunch of blooms has been left to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns IE + L backwards, which suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland of blossoms worn round the neck is a strung collection of flowers.

clue.text: Greedy person a long time finding contents of pies?

parts.note: a pig is a glutton
eons are vast ages, a long time

explanation.surface: A glutton taking ages to discover what is inside some pies.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: pigeon pie is a traditional dish.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds are a traditional filling for game pies, so they can be what is inside them.

clue.text: Bears introducing component of atmosphere — into these?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the air that is breathed goes into these organs

indicators.note: the bears word takes something new inside it, letting it in

parts.note: lugs means carries or bears something heavy
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, the main gas in air

explanation.surface: Animals letting some air in, and asking where that air ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question pointing at where breathed air goes, so the whole clue reads as a description of breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaled air passes into the pair of breathing organs in the chest, which is what the question hints at.

clue.text: Bad smell surrounding couple (including boy) producing pollution

indicators.note: the bad smell goes all round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: pong is British slang for a stink

indicators.note: the couple holds the boy within it

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A foul odour around a pair and their son is creating contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' is the Roman numeral for two, split open by the boy under 'including'; 'surrounding' then wraps the smell round that whole unit, making ISONI its filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Poisoning of land, air or water by toxins is a form of pollution; the two can be used interchangeably.

clue.text: Clever book offering the correct opinion?

parts.note: the right view is the correct one

explanation.surface: A smart volume that presents the proper point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright pupil is a clever one; the two are everyday synonyms for intelligent.

clue.text: Argument after endless decline in singing voice

indicators.note: the argument piece comes after the shortened decline piece in the answer
the decline word loses its final letter

parts.note: a fall is a decline
a set-to is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A row following a long slump in a singer's high register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the decline word, and 'after' places the argument behind it; a set-to is a British term for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register a male singer uses above his natural range.

clue.text: Supporting the old ways? Time to take on Latin radio broadcast

indicators.note: the time letter takes on the following letters, adding them after it
scattered widely, so the letters are spread about anew

explanation.surface: A conservative station deciding it is time to air Latin programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges LATIN RADIO into RADITIONAL, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conservative who adheres to long-established customs is traditional in outlook.

clue.text: A habit you may get into while trekking

definitions.text: A habit you may get into while trekking

parts.words: A habit you may get into while trekking
parts.note: habit here is clothing (as a nun's habit), not a routine, and the trek is across the African bush

explanation.surface: Advice about a routine a hiker might fall into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into a habit' suggests forming a routine; here habit means an outfit, and the trek is an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: A belted, pocketed khaki jacket and trousers outfit worn for expeditions in the African bush.

clue.text: Mean chap's cuddled by drunk in game

indicators.note: the drunk wraps arms round the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
low means mean or base
his means belonging to a chap

explanation.surface: A miserly fellow gets hugged by a drunk during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddled by' has the drunk wrap round both the mean word and the chap's; solo whist is a British pub and family card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game, a variant of whist in which players bid for tricks alone.

clue.text: Revolutionary periods confuse on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, so the word for confuse is given by its sound

parts.note: to daze is to stun or confuse

explanation.surface: A broadcast that muddles listeners about turbulent eras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests uprisings, but a day is one turn of the Earth on its axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Each 24-hour unit is the time the planet takes to spin once, a period defined by rotation.

clue.text: Person looking to make a profit very engaged by one source of wise counsel

definitions.text: Person looking to make a profit

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the very letter is taken on within the other pieces, held inside them

parts.note: Nestor was the wise old adviser to the Greeks at Troy

explanation.surface: A profit-seeker hiring a sage adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: NESTOR is the elderly Greek king in Homer famed for advice; V goes inside I + NESTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor puts money into ventures in the hope of a return, seeking gains.

clue.text: Original idea to dismiss first reserve?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the idea word is sent away

parts.note: a spark is the first flash of an idea

explanation.surface: A manager's novel plan to sack the first-choice substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' looks like a substitute player; the question mark flags a nature reserve sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park is a protected area of land, much like a nature reserve.

clue.text: Early arrival about to get space in confusion

indicators.note: the about and space pieces sit inside the confusion word

parts.note: pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type, a confusion
re means about, concerning
an em is a printing space

explanation.surface: Someone turning up early is about to find room amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE (also spelt pi) is a printer's mess of type; EM is a printer's space.
explanation.definitionFit: A preemie is an informal word for a baby born before term.

clue.text: Temperate tree yielding soft fruit

parts.note: clement means mild, of weather

indicators.note: the tree gives up a letter, surrendering it

parts.note: a pine is a tree
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A tree in a mild climate bearing gentle fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding' takes P (soft, piano) out of PINE to leave INE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, easily peeled citrus fruit, a cross between a mandarin and an orange.

clue.text: Observe cut limiting firm with record in green issues

indicators.note: the shortened observe word confines the other pieces inside
the observe word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to eye is to observe
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a log is a record

explanation.surface: Watch the cuts restricting a business with a track record on the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the observe word, and 'limiting' has what remains hold the firm and record; 'green' means environmental, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology, the study of living things and their surroundings, is also used for environmental concerns.

clue.text: Supervision spurned by a revolutionary nursery

indicators.note: the a is rejected, pushed out of the supervision word

parts.note: care is supervision or looking after
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel rejecting looking after children in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurned by a' removes A from CARE to leave CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where young children are looked after.

clue.text: They may show surprise I sample books audibly

indicators.note: the phrase is said out loud and heard as another phrase

parts.note: to browse books is to dip into them, so the phrase is 'I browse'

explanation.surface: Someone startled while dipping into volumes in a bookshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised facial hair above the eyes is a classic sign of astonishment.

clue.text: Only partially warmer in ordinary wool

indicators.note: Only partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A garment is only somewhat warmer than an ordinary woollen one.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a fine soft fleece from a breed of sheep, a type of wool.

clue.text: Inordinately pleased — having upped sticks?

indicators.note: in a down answer the word goes up, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: Someone very satisfied about having moved house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped sticks' is a British idiom for moving home, but here sticks is a verb (glues) and upped reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes excessive self-satisfaction, being far too pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Perverted pleasure taken from correcting his commas

indicators.note: putting the punctuation right rearranges these letters

explanation.surface: A pedant's twisted delight in fixing someone's punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Deriving pleasure, often sexual, from one's own pain or humiliation is a recognised perversion.

clue.text: Appear to miss latest match

indicators.note: the appear word goes without its last letter

parts.note: to seem is to appear

explanation.surface: Turning up just too late for the most recent game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game; in poker, to see a bet is to match it.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, calling a stake equal to an opponent's is to match their bet.

clue.text: Dance in South America — recollection of summer that has to fade

parts.note: a suntan is a reminder of summer days
to go is to fade or disappear

explanation.surface: A dancer in Argentina whose holiday glow is wearing off.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is the ballroom dance that originated in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

clue.text: Component set to roll over, trapping soldiers

indicators.note: the reversed set word holds the soldiers inside it
the set word turns over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: tele is short for a television set
men are soldiers, ordinary ranks

explanation.surface: A part that is ready to tumble, catching some troops underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a television, not a verb; 'to roll over' gives ELET, and 'trapping' has that hold the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a constituent part of something, the same as a component.

clue.text: Tree knocked over is framed by bloody artist

indicators.note: the reversed tree sits inside the bloody word as if in a frame

parts.note: gory means bloody

indicators.note: the tree falls over, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A felled tree surrounded by carnage in some grim artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns the tree word round, and 'is framed by' sets it inside the bloody word; Gormley is a famous British sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony Gormley is the British sculptor behind the Angel of the North.
